seoTitle: Inventory Turnover and Days of Inventory Calculator
metaDescription: Compute turnover and days of inventory from cost of goods sold and opening and closing inventory. Free, private.
intro: Calculates how many times stock turns over in a period and how many days it sits.
why:
Turnover shows how fast stock sells. Too low means cash sits on shelves, and too high can mean lost sales from stock-outs. Dividing by 365 gives days of inventory, which is easier to read.

Use cost of goods sold, not revenue, and inventory valued at cost so both sides share a basis. What counts as a good value differs a lot between products, so compare with your own past figures and similar businesses.
howTo: Enter cost of goods sold for the period.
Enter inventory value at the start and end.
Set days in the period and read turnover and days.

faq.a: Stock changes during the period, so averaging start and end smooths it.

faq.q: Can I use revenue instead of COGS?
faq.a: Not for the standard ratio. It mixes cost and price bases.
It depends on the product. Compare with your history and peers.
